about: The in-scope capability-manifest rows dart_monty_core's M3 owns, each with the backends it must be PRESENT on (tool/parity/score.py --target; shown, not asserted, until --assert-target lands at the cut). Every in-scope manifest row is in `rows` or in `excluded` with the clause that excludes it; `judgement` ids point at the rows the rule did not decide mechanically (the owner-reviewed list). An `allowed` entry names why a target row may be non-PRESENT; it is valid only as the approved rule or an owner-approved exception says, and is stale (fails) once its row is PRESENT on those backends. An `allowed` entry may carry `evidenced_by`: the core tests that evidence a row no binding exposes ({path, tests, exercises}; score.py --target --core DIR checks each file and test title exists). The owner's P-t decisions (PT1, 2026-10-14) are applied: J08's host_callback_authority and cpython_value_adapter are allowed N/A; J10's four protocol rows are allowed N/A, each evidenced by core's worker-channel tests and E0; protocol_value_arena, unstable_graph_access and timezone_database are mapped to worker cases (tool/parity/rows.json, `worker`).

A1.text: area filesystem: mounts and the memory filesystem are M6 (C0a)

A3.text: area deployment: prebuilt workers and delivery

A4.text: area runtime_cli: the upstream command line

B1.text: os_calls row whose every parity case needs a mounted filesystem (rows.json case sets `fs`)

C1.text: upstream lacks the row in its bindings: neither python_cite nor js_cite in the manifest, and no parity case, probe, worker set or session rule compares it against the python binding (a Rust-API oracle does not count)

G7.text: browser aggregate-memory resource_limits rows (M6, G7): the web backends are not targets for the row, the native backend is

D1.text: standalone type checking: the rule makes only type_checking in the session a target; M6 removes standalone typeCheck

D2.text: upstream has no behaviour to compare: the C1 gate records it as core-gated (c1-gate.json core_gated), upstream's sinks and cancellation are its binding's own

allowed.reason: No binding exposes framing and no python-binding oracle compares it. Core evidences the row with its own worker-channel tests: the frame codec and decode budget in Dart (pure Dart, so on all three backends), the VM channel against a fake worker process, the web connection against a fake port, and one round trip through the real worker; and with E0 through the worker (tool/parity/e0.json, run against the real worker on vm, dart2js and dart2wasm in the `e0` CI job). Not covered by a named test: a body of exactly the maximum size is never fed (only its length prefix).
allowed.cite: owner decision PT1, 2026-10-14 (P-t review, J08 and J10)

evidenced_by.exercises: the Dart frame codec: the 4-byte little-endian prefix, an outbound body over the maximum refused, a stream cut inside a body truncated, an oversize prefix refused; the maximum is exercised as a length prefix only (pure Dart: VM, dart2js, dart2wasm)

is upstream DEFAULT_MAX_DECODE_BYTES
evidenced_by.exercises: the Dart frame scanner's decode budget: upstream's DEFAULT_MAX_DECODE_BYTES and a boundary frame that charges one slot over it, refused before anything is reserved

tests: an oversize length prefix desynchronises: worker killed
a torn frame is vanished, naming the truncation
evidenced_by.exercises: ProcessChannel (VM) against a fake worker process: a torn frame or an oversize prefix from the worker is a typed crash

tests: a torn reply is a vanished crash
an oversized request is refused before it is posted
evidenced_by.exercises: the web connection against a fake port: a torn reply is a crash; an oversized request is refused before it is posted and the channel stays usable

allowed.reason: Upstream runs the worker dispatcher in Rust (Child, SessionBudget, dispatch_frame); no binding exposes it and no python-binding oracle compares it. Core evidences the row with its worker-channel tests: the real worker executable (the Configure, Feed, Shutdown lifecycle, in-band errors, the suspension and sleep budgets), the VM channel and web connection against fakes (fatal, shutdown, one turn at a time), the Dart budget accounting, and the driver over a scripted channel; and with E0 through the worker (tool/parity/e0.json, run against the real worker on vm, dart2js and dart2wasm in the `e0` CI job). The Rust dispatcher is reached only through the real-worker tests and E0.
allowed.cite: owner decision PT1, 2026-10-14 (P-t review, J08 and J10)

allowed.reason: Rust-domain/protobuf conversion and validation is not exposed by any binding. Core evidences the row with its arena and host-answer tests (Dart conversion, against upstream-generated golden bytes and local tables), the driver over a scripted channel, and real-worker conversions of integers and floats; and with E0 through the worker (tool/parity/e0.json, run against the real worker on vm, dart2js and dart2wasm in the `e0` CI job). Rust's semantic validation failures (ProtoConvertError paths) are reached only through the real-worker tests and E0.
allowed.cite: owner decision PT1, 2026-10-14 (P-t review, J08 and J10)

allowed.reason: The declared check (current and minimum 5) is not exposed by a binding. Core evidences the row with tests that send the protocol version on Configure and refuse a skewed worker: the real worker accepts 5 and refuses 999 with a FatalError and exit 4; the web channels refuse a worker that reports 4 or none before any request. Not covered by a named test: a version below the minimum sent to the real worker (the Rust check), which the web handshake tests replace with a fabricated ready message.
allowed.cite: owner decision PT1, 2026-10-14 (P-t review, J08 and J10)

Configure, Feed 1 + 1, Shutdown
evidenced_by.exercises: the real worker (VM): protocol version 5 is accepted; 999 is a FatalError and exit 4

a ready reply without a protocol is skew
evidenced_by.exercises: the web connection refuses a ready message reporting protocol 4, or none, before any request

tests: a protocol mismatch is refused before Configure
evidenced_by.exercises: a stand-in Web Worker reporting protocol 4 is refused before Configure (dart2js and dart2wasm)

tests: Configure carries the protocol version, name and limits
a FatalError answer (version skew) is a crash
evidenced_by.exercises: Configure carries the version; a scripted version-skew FatalError is a typed crash

tests: a refused Configure frees the slot and throws
evidenced_by.exercises: a scripted refused Configure frees its pool slot and throws (the pool, not the version check)
